newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares edge down at noon in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares edge down at noon in slow trade.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B share index eased at midday on Tuesday, pulled down by steep falls in a handful of third-liners amid sporadic trading, brokers said.
The B share index inched down 0.25 points or 0.16 percent to 148.87 on turnover of HK$28 million.

The domestic A share index fell 7.22 points or 1.63 percent to 435.90, ending a brief rally starting from last Friday after heavy losses caused by Beijing's moves to squeeze out excessive speculation, brokers said.
Turnover on Tuesday morning was 3.4 billion yuan.

"Light selling in several cheap-priced B share issues drove them down sharply and trimmed the B share index," a broker at a Chinese brokerage said. "But the fall is insignificant in light of their thin volumes."
Shenzhen Petrochemical Co was the worst B share performer, diving HK$0.31 or 8.93 percent to HK$3.16 after just 5,776 shares changed hands.
Liquidity mainly flowed towards recently listed big-capitalisation counters, with Beijing Orient Electronics Co the most actively traded on volume of 1.8 million shares and rose HK$0.17 to HK$4.35.
Brokers said the B share market is likely to maintain narrow-band movement in the next few sessions, with the direction of the A shares unclear.
"Given the ban on state banks and enterprises and listed firms trading shares, it will be hard for the market to regain its bullishness," an analyst with Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
Tight-range fluctuation is expected in the afternoon, brokers said.

Newcomer chemical concern Beijing Huaer was the sharpest loser in the A share market. It dropped 1.27 yuan or 9.08 percent to 12.72 yuan due to profit-taking after a solid debut on Monday, brokers said.
